database:primary-key:user.decision: One User entity keyed by an opaque random text id (uuid4 hex) generated by the unified app; A's integer ids and B's 'lu-<n>' ids are not reused (no persisted source data exists; a legacy_id would hold them if data were ever imported).

database:field-type:user.id.decision: User.id is text (uuid4 hex) for every user; see database:primary-key:user.

database:field-meaning:user.id.decision: Neither source id survives: A's counter and B's 'lu-' counter are both replaced by one generated opaque id; the meaning is 'the unified user's id'.

database:field-meaning:user.email.decision: User.email is the person's normalised (trimmed, lowercased) email. A's lowercased key and B's provider email are kept apart from ownership: a PasswordCredential owns its email (unique), a federated Identity records the provider's email and whether it was verified; only owned emails are used for linking.

database:nullability:user.email.decision: User.email optional (a provider may send none); password users always have one; a federated sign-in without an email never links.

database:enum:user.role.decision: One value set: viewer, editor, admin. Mapping A user->editor, B member->viewer, C roles unchanged (user decision in task.md); unknown source roles raise KeyError.

database:default-value:user.role.decision: Default role depends on how the account was created: password registration gets map_source_role('A','user') = editor; a new federated account gets map_source_role('B','member') = viewer (user decision).

application:business-rule:default_role.decision: Same as database:default-value:user.role: editor for password sign-up, viewer for a new federated account; a linked federated sign-in keeps the existing account's role.

application:business-rule:email_case.decision: Emails are normalised everywhere (strip, lowercase) before storage, lookup and linking; B's as-given emails are normalised.

database:duplicate-entity:user.decision: Merge A:User and B:Account into one User (alias recorded with reason); sign-in methods become child records: PasswordCredential (A's email, salt, hash) and Identity (B's provider, subject, email, email_verified).

database:deletion-semantics:user.decision: No delete feature is kept in either source slice and none is built; deletion is out of scope (recorded in the PRD). If added later: hard delete plus session revocation.

application:auth-provider:provider.decision: One identity system (the unified identity module) with two sign-in methods: local password and a federated OAuth provider behind an adapter; the provider callback data (provider, subject, email, email_verified) is the input to login_oauth. Real provider token verification is not testable here.

application:auth-methods:methods.decision: Offer both kept methods, password and OAuth, through the one identity system.

application:session:session.decision: One session mechanism: an opaque random token (secrets.token_urlsafe(32)) stored only as its SHA-256, with an expiry (default 8 h, configurable), revocable by logout; both sign-in methods issue it. A web layer would carry it in an http-only secure cookie.

application:authorization-model:model.decision: One role-based model (C's): roles viewer/editor/admin as permission sets and one can(role, permission) check used by every privileged action.

application:roles:roles.decision: One role set (viewer, editor, admin) with role_mapping A:user->editor, B:member->viewer, C:viewer/editor/admin unchanged (user decision). Special powers stay permissions (manage_roles).

application:identity-linking:accounts.decision: User decision: one account per person; a federated sign-in joins an existing account only when the provider says email_verified is exactly True and the email is owned by an existing account; otherwise it is a separate account. Never link on an unverified email.

application:workflow:duplicate-registrat.decision: Refuse registration when the normalised email is already owned by an account (password or verified federated); raise AuthError and never overwrite.

application:permission:role-change-rules.decision: set_role(token, user_id, role): caller resolved from the session; PermissionError unless the caller is admin (invalid session included); role must be a known unified role (ValueError); target must exist (KeyError); nobody may raise their own role (PermissionError) (user decision).

application:workflow:first-admin.decision: bootstrap_admin(email, password) creates the first admin for setup only and is refused (PermissionError) once any admin exists.

migration:user.decision: Plan approved: the sources keep their data only in process memory, so there is no persisted source data to migrate and no migration will run. If data is imported later: re-key to new ids with legacy_id, map roles by role_mapping, normalise emails; that run needs its own migration approval, a backup and a dry run.

migration:passwordcredential.decision: Plan approved: A.User/B.Account id and role are not dropped; they move to the unified User row (id re-keyed with legacy_id, role mapped by role_mapping). No persisted source data exists, so nothing runs; any later import needs its own migration approval.

migration:identity.decision: Plan approved: A.User/B.Account id and role are not dropped; they move to the unified User row (id re-keyed with legacy_id, role mapped by role_mapping). No persisted source data exists, so nothing runs; any later import needs its own migration approval.

migration:session.decision: Not run: sessions are not migrated (in-memory, users sign in again).
